summary.oneLiner: One year post-listing, the model is doing what it promised: revenue INR 546 cr (+44% YoY), normalized EBITDA INR 107 cr (+74% YoY) with margin expanding to 19.6%, and normalized PAT nearly tripling to INR 39 cr — the fifth consecutive quarter of sequential improvement across revenue, EBITDA, margin, PAT and ROCE. This was also the heaviest capex quarter in the company's history, and the central claim being tested is that new capex cycles are no longer margin-dilutive because each cohort lands on a larger mature base. Guidance reaffirmed at 28–30% revenue growth, 19–20% margin and over 13 mn sq ft operational by March 2027.

financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q1 FY27 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | INR 546 cr | +44% | +5% QoQ |
| Normalized EBITDA / margin | INR 107 cr / 19.6% | +74% | +8% QoQ; margin 16.2% in Q1FY26, 19% in Q4FY26 |
| Normalized PAT | INR 39 cr | from INR 13 cr | +11% QoQ; EBITDA-to-PAT gap narrowing as centres mature |
| Order book (contracted revenue) | ~INR 5,400 cr committed | — | 87% of FY27 revenue already contracted |
| Cash / net debt | Net debt INR 5.6 cr — virtually debt-free | — | Borrowing cost under 9%; credit rating upgraded earlier this year |
| ROCE (annualised) | 21.5% | +870 bps | Held flat through the heaviest investment quarter; INR 151 cr fresh capital deployed |
> Operating: total area ~17 mn sq ft, operational 10.4 mn sq ft, 760+ clients, 150,000+ professionals. Occupancy 81% vs 82% in Q4FY26 — purely new-building fill. Mature centres 89% occupancy on 9.1 mn sq ft with committed occupancy 92%. Seat retention 74%, but occupied seats *rose* during the quarter. Multi-city clients 35% of revenue (31% in FY26); 1,000+ seater cohort 41% (37%); GCC clients 21% (15%); IT/ITES down to 35% (44% FY24 → 42% FY25 → 39% FY26). Realisation INR 181/sq ft on incremental mature-footprint seats vs ~INR 170 in the prior fiscal. Non-lease rental revenue INR 68 cr vs INR 22 cr a year ago. Cash: OCF/EBITDA 0.9x on normalized OCF of INR 95 cr (+10% YoY) — the dip is INR 33 cr of security deposits paid to landlords to book FY28/FY29 buildings. FCF −INR 56 cr (vs −INR 4.9 cr) as capex stepped up 66% YoY to ~INR 150 cr, of which INR 45 cr into upcoming centres. Negative working capital with ~six days debtors.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue growth:** FY27 **reaffirmed at 28% to 30%**. Management defended the apparent conservatism directly — with committed occupancy at 92% there is little to sell on the existing base, so growth depends on new centres that take ~12 months to ramp: "you will see maybe Q3 or mostly Q4 see that jump."
- **Margin:** normalized EBITDA margin **19% to 20%** for the full year.
- **Footprint:** operational footprint of **over 13 mn sq ft by March 2027**, i.e. 2.5–3.0 mn sq ft added in FY27. Already 3.5 mn sq ft signed and under or entering construction — a buffer of 700,000–800,000 sq ft against project delays. 1.9 mn sq ft currently under fit-out.
- **Capex:** **INR 550–600 cr for FY27**, covering both fresh fit-outs and the three-yearly refurbishment cycle. New fit-out capex INR 1,350/sq ft, rising ~5% a year on inflation; refurbishment ~15% of initial capex every three years.
- **Occupancy:** "anywhere between 80% to 85% is where we can effectively look at our occupancies throughout the next three quarters, despite the high growth."
- **ROCE:** expected to expand meaningfully through FY28 as the current capex cohort matures and completes payback.
- **SmartVantage / VAS:** services revenue expected to "meaningfully double over the next two years" — but explicitly **not** factored into current-year projections.
- **Commissioning:** ~3 mn sq ft comes online over the next nine months, including Eastbridge (Vikhroli, Mumbai — 8.15 lakh sq ft, claimed as the world's largest standalone managed campus) and Eastside (Pune), both landing in H2 FY27 with strong pre-fills.
order book & pipeline: The annuity structure is the asset: clients sign four-to-five year agreements, committed contracted revenue is ~INR 5,400 cr, and 87% of FY27 revenue is already contracted. Supply-side visibility is equally forward — every building needed for the next two years is secured and work on FY29 has begun, with long-term rights giving "uninterrupted access to quality buildings for the next 10 to 15 years." Roughly 30–35% of any new building is pre-committed by existing clients before it is taken, driven by the multi-city flywheel. Historical ramp is 80–85% occupancy within 13–14 months, and management says that has held even as building sizes grew from 300,000–400,000 sq ft to 600,000–700,000 sq ft.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **India core rental (~92% of rental revenue is enterprise annuity demand):** 1,000+ seat cohort on 48-month tenures expanding across cities. Client mix deliberately diversified away from IT/ITES toward manufacturing, engineering, business consultancy and professional services; the stated target range for IT/ITES is 25–35%.
- **GCC:** 21% of revenue from 15% in FY26, described as the primary growth driver for the next two to three years. Clients now include a large Swiss bank, a manufacturing GCC and, this quarter, the subsidiary of a leading Japanese NBFC at the Mumbai campus. Demand is broadening beyond the US into Europe and Japan.
- **Value-added services / SmartVantage:** non-lease rental revenue tripled to INR 68 cr from INR 22 cr. Two large SmartVantage contracts won. Critically, the model is **take-rate based** — third parties provide the service, Smartworks takes a cut with no expense on its books, so it flows straight to the bottom line.
- **Singapore:** Work Studio acquired at cost of construction (it was at ~60% occupancy); Singapore now ~1,500 seats, ~80,000 sq ft, ~2% of revenue, with 400–450 seats available to sell. Explicitly not a scale market — "Not meaningfully… it's not going to go from 80,000 to 160,000 or 200,000." Funded entirely from Singapore cash flows with no risk on the Indian balance sheet.
growth verticals / optionality: Two demand engines were laid out and both are already in the client base rather than prospective. First, flex is consolidating: India recorded its highest ever quarterly leasing at 24.6 mn sq ft with 27% through flex (up from 19% a year ago), and within flex the top-10 operators' share climbed from 67% in 2024 to 72% in 2025 and 74% in H1 of this year, with the long tail below 5% and shrinking. Second, AI and GCCs are expanding office demand outright — the AI workforce inside India's GCCs is set to grow fourfold by 2030, and that demand lands in exactly the collaboration-rich campuses Smartworks builds. Management's summary arithmetic: commercial real estate growing >6%, flex growing 23%, Smartworks growing 44% — "roughly seven times the office market and twice the Flex market."
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Scale as the price of entry:** "Scale, balance sheet strength, and developer relations are now the price of entry, and smaller players simply cannot add buildings the way large platforms can." At 10.4 mn sq ft operational the company claims the largest platform in the industry, earning preferred landlord terms and lower unit costs.
- **Getting the right building first:** "For the past 4 to 5 years, demand for office space in our micro-markets has outpaced the availability of new office buildings. In a market running short of quality office supply, getting the right building first is the biggest advantage."
- **Institutional developer relationships as a completion hedge:** over the last 12–18 months the platform has attracted DLF, Hiranandani, Tata, Panchshil and Salarpuria — "These are the partners who deliver on schedule as well, and that is where the developer relationship is precisely the hedge that we have against any completion risk."
- **Downside resilience, evidenced:** committed client lock-ins cover landlord rental commitments roughly two times over at portfolio level; no single client typically takes more than 30% of a campus; asset-liability mismatch eliminated up to FY29; and "Through every cycle since inception, we have not surrendered a single campus."
- **Pricing headroom held back deliberately:** realisation is INR 181/sq ft while "the closest competitor is almost 10% to 15% higher than our numbers" — a stated, unused lever.
margins & cost dynamics: Margin expanded to 19.6% from 16.2% a year ago on three drivers: centre maturity, cost-excellence initiatives particularly in energy (solar adoption across campuses), and operating leverage at both centre and corporate level. The structural claim is the one to test: "Each new investment cycle lands on a larger, mature near-fixed-cost base. So, every new cohort is smaller relative to that base, and its ramp-up drag keeps shrinking. At our current scale, adding new centres and the associated capex is simply not margin dilutive." Once a centre crosses breakeven, incremental revenue flows disproportionately to EBITDA. VAS is margin-accretive by construction because of the take-rate model.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): INR 550–600 cr planned for FY27 against INR 388 cr last year, with ~INR 150 cr already spent in Q1 (up 66% YoY). The pipeline is over-provisioned by design: 3.5 mn sq ft signed against a 2.5–3.0 mn sq ft addition target, so a one-to-two quarter delay on any project can be absorbed by another asset. Management builds a one-to-two quarter buffer into every handover assumption. The two marquee H2 FY27 assets — Eastbridge (Vikhroli) and Eastside (Pune) — are the specific slippage risk since both land in the second half and both are large.
capital allocation: Growth is self-funded by design: negative working capital, ~six days debtors, float income from tenant security deposits, and net debt of just INR 5.6 cr. India cash flows are deployed into the domestic platform; international growth funds itself from international cash flows — the Work Studio acquisition was paid for entirely out of Singapore-generated cash. The INR 33 cr of security deposits paid to landlords this quarter is capital allocated to securing FY28 and FY29 supply — "We are paying today to own tomorrow's growth."
risks & watch-items:
- **Seat retention of 74% is the number that will be picked at.** Management's defence is that churn is deliberate portfolio rebalancing and mark-to-market repricing, that occupied seats rose, and that committed occupancy of mature centres remains 92% because replacement tenants are already found. Last year's full-year retention was 80–88% after a similarly weak first half.
- Occupancy dipped to 81% from 82% and is guided to 80–85% for three quarters — new-building fill, but it caps the reported metric during the heaviest growth phase.
- FCF is negative INR 56 cr and OCF/EBITDA fell below 1x. Both are explained by growth investment, but they are the first negative prints since listing.
- Concentration in H2: the guidance depends on Eastbridge and Eastside landing on schedule and pre-fills converting.
- Client-mix transition is deliberate but ongoing — IT/ITES fell from 44% to 35% over three years, and management could not break out call-centre exposure within IT/ITES when asked about AI-driven renewal risk.
- The margin-not-dilutive-at-scale claim has only been tested through one heavy capex quarter.
management quality / tone: Confident and unusually well-instrumented — the team quoted third-party market data (Cushman & Wakefield flex-share series), gave a specific realisation number (INR 181/sq ft vs INR 170 prior year) unprompted, and directed analysts to specific presentation slides repeatedly. Notably, the transcript carries **nine numbered footnote corrections** where management corrected its own misstatements on the call (occupancy figures, seat counts, retention wording, an incorrectly named asset) — a level of transcript hygiene that is itself a governance signal. Neetish Sarda answered the conservatism challenge on guidance head-on rather than accepting the flattery. Harsh Binani was explicit that VAS upside is *not* in the numbers, which is the right way to handle an unproven line.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The retention/occupancy pair must be read together: a 74% retention number alongside 92% committed occupancy and rising occupied seats means the company is actively repricing legacy tenants out, not losing them involuntarily. The metric will look bad in H1 and recover by year-end, as it did last year.
- VAS is structurally more attractive than it looks because it is take-rate, not resale — no cost sits on the books, so it hits the bottom line directly. It tripled YoY and is explicitly excluded from guidance.
- The GCC revenue already booked understates the opportunity: the services layer for signed GCCs has not started billing because most offices are still under fit-out — "the value accretion of the other services over and above the space will happen… over the next two or three quarters."
- Management is holding back a 10–15% pricing lever versus the nearest competitor, choosing volume and campus fill over rate.
- Landlord mix is ~65% non-institutional / 35% institutional and is expected to stay roughly there — the institutional share is the completion hedge, not the whole strategy.

themes.title: Flexible workspace, PropTech & commercial real-estate services

hero.oneLiner: One year post-listing, the model is doing what it promised: revenue INR 546 cr (+44% YoY), normalized EBITDA INR 107 cr (+74% YoY) with margin expanding to 19.6%, and normalized PAT nearly tripling to INR 39 cr — the fifth consecutive quarter of sequential improvement across revenue, EBITDA, margin, PAT and ROCE. This was also the heaviest capex quarter in the company's history, and the central claim being tested is that new capex cycles are no longer margin-dilutive because each cohort lands on a larger mature base. Guidance reaffirmed at 28–30% revenue growth, 19–20% margin and over 13 mn sq ft operational by March 2027.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Claims to be the "Only listed platform to cross 10 Msf operational SBA", with "Undisputed Leadership In West And North India" and total SBA of 16.9 Msf across 70 centres and 15 cities (India + Singapore), 381k capacity seats.
- Enterprise-led, not startup-led: ~92% of rental revenue from enterprise clients (Fortune 500, Forbes 2000, MNCs and Indian conglomerates); ~41% from the 1,000+ seat cohort (up from ~37% in FY26) and ~35% from multi-city clients (up from ~31% in FY26).
- Model is a "one-stop solution" — full-building leases with guaranteed rentals to non-institutional landlords, and "One contract, one SLA, one invoice" for enterprise clients, live in 45-60 days.
- Flywheel framing: "Scale enables better terms; better terms enable more scale" — office space demand, availability, margin expansion and cash-to-RoCE uplift reinforcing each other; "At scale, flex becomes an infrastructure business where execution and capital efficiency win."
- Deck argues early access to Grade-A campuses is "the single biggest moat" in an office-space-constrained market, with its own campuses "secured through FY28, partially FY29".

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **India core rental (~92% of rental revenue is enterprise annuity demand):** 1,000+ seat cohort on 48-month tenures expanding across cities. Client mix deliberately diversified away from IT/ITES toward manufacturing, engineering, business consultancy and professional services; the stated target range for IT/ITES is 25–35%.
- **GCC:** 21% of revenue from 15% in FY26, described as the primary growth driver for the next two to three years. Clients now include a large Swiss bank, a manufacturing GCC and, this quarter, the subsidiary of a leading Japanese NBFC at the Mumbai campus. Demand is broadening beyond the US into Europe and Japan.
- **Value-added services / SmartVantage:** non-lease rental revenue tripled to INR 68 cr from INR 22 cr. Two large SmartVantage contracts won. Critically, the model is **take-rate based** — third parties provide the service, Smartworks takes a cut with no expense on its books, so it flows straight to the bottom line.
- **Singapore:** Work Studio acquired at cost of construction (it was at ~60% occupancy); Singapore now ~1,500 seats, ~80,000 sq ft, ~2% of revenue, with 400–450 seats available to sell. Explicitly not a scale market — "Not meaningfully… it's not going to go from 80,000 to 160,000 or 200,000." Funded entirely from Singapore cash flows with no risk on the Indian balance sheet.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: The annuity structure is the asset: clients sign four-to-five year agreements, committed contracted revenue is ~INR 5,400 cr, and 87% of FY27 revenue is already contracted. Supply-side visibility is equally forward — every building needed for the next two years is secured and work on FY29 has begun, with long-term rights giving "uninterrupted access to quality buildings for the next 10 to 15 years." Roughly 30–35% of any new building is pre-committed by existing clients before it is taken, driven by the multi-city flywheel. Historical ramp is 80–85% occupancy within 13–14 months, and management says that has held even as building sizes grew from 300,000–400,000 sq ft to 600,000–700,000 sq ft.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Revenue growth:** FY27 **reaffirmed at 28% to 30%**. Management defended the apparent conservatism directly — with committed occupancy at 92% there is little to sell on the existing base, so growth depends on new centres that take ~12 months to ramp: "you will see maybe Q3 or mostly Q4 see that jump."
- **Margin:** normalized EBITDA margin **19% to 20%** for the full year.
- **Footprint:** operational footprint of **over 13 mn sq ft by March 2027**, i.e. 2.5–3.0 mn sq ft added in FY27. Already 3.5 mn sq ft signed and under or entering construction — a buffer of 700,000–800,000 sq ft against project delays. 1.9 mn sq ft currently under fit-out.
- **Capex:** **INR 550–600 cr for FY27**, covering both fresh fit-outs and the three-yearly refurbishment cycle. New fit-out capex INR 1,350/sq ft, rising ~5% a year on inflation; refurbishment ~15% of initial capex every three years.
- **Occupancy:** "anywhere between 80% to 85% is where we can effectively look at our occupancies throughout the next three quarters, despite the high growth."
- **ROCE:** expected to expand meaningfully through FY28 as the current capex cohort matures and completes payback.
- **SmartVantage / VAS:** services revenue expected to "meaningfully double over the next two years" — but explicitly **not** factored into current-year projections.
- **Commissioning:** ~3 mn sq ft comes online over the next nine months, including Eastbridge (Vikhroli, Mumbai — 8.15 lakh sq ft, claimed as the world's largest standalone managed campus) and Eastside (Pune), both landing in H2 FY27 with strong pre-fills.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Two demand engines were laid out and both are already in the client base rather than prospective. First, flex is consolidating: India recorded its highest ever quarterly leasing at 24.6 mn sq ft with 27% through flex (up from 19% a year ago), and within flex the top-10 operators' share climbed from 67% in 2024 to 72% in 2025 and 74% in H1 of this year, with the long tail below 5% and shrinking. Second, AI and GCCs are expanding office demand outright — the AI workforce inside India's GCCs is set to grow fourfold by 2030, and that demand lands in exactly the collaboration-rich campuses Smartworks builds. Management's summary arithmetic: commercial real estate growing >6%, flex growing 23%, Smartworks growing 44% — "roughly seven times the office market and twice the Flex market."

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Margin expanded to 19.6% from 16.2% a year ago on three drivers: centre maturity, cost-excellence initiatives particularly in energy (solar adoption across campuses), and operating leverage at both centre and corporate level. The structural claim is the one to test: "Each new investment cycle lands on a larger, mature near-fixed-cost base. So, every new cohort is smaller relative to that base, and its ramp-up drag keeps shrinking. At our current scale, adding new centres and the associated capex is simply not margin dilutive." Once a centre crosses breakeven, incremental revenue flows disproportionately to EBITDA. VAS is margin-accretive by construction because of the take-rate model.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Growth is self-funded by design: negative working capital, ~six days debtors, float income from tenant security deposits, and net debt of just INR 5.6 cr. India cash flows are deployed into the domestic platform; international growth funds itself from international cash flows — the Work Studio acquisition was paid for entirely out of Singapore-generated cash. The INR 33 cr of security deposits paid to landlords this quarter is capital allocated to securing FY28 and FY29 supply — "We are paying today to own tomorrow's growth."

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and unusually well-instrumented — the team quoted third-party market data (Cushman & Wakefield flex-share series), gave a specific realisation number (INR 181/sq ft vs INR 170 prior year) unprompted, and directed analysts to specific presentation slides repeatedly. Notably, the transcript carries **nine numbered footnote corrections** where management corrected its own misstatements on the call (occupancy figures, seat counts, retention wording, an incorrectly named asset) — a level of transcript hygiene that is itself a governance signal. Neetish Sarda answered the conservatism challenge on guidance head-on rather than accepting the flattery. Harsh Binani was explicit that VAS upside is *not* in the numbers, which is the right way to handle an unproven line.

moat.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position
moat.body:
- **Scale as the price of entry:** "Scale, balance sheet strength, and developer relations are now the price of entry, and smaller players simply cannot add buildings the way large platforms can." At 10.4 mn sq ft operational the company claims the largest platform in the industry, earning preferred landlord terms and lower unit costs.
- **Getting the right building first:** "For the past 4 to 5 years, demand for office space in our micro-markets has outpaced the availability of new office buildings. In a market running short of quality office supply, getting the right building first is the biggest advantage."
- **Institutional developer relationships as a completion hedge:** over the last 12–18 months the platform has attracted DLF, Hiranandani, Tata, Panchshil and Salarpuria — "These are the partners who deliver on schedule as well, and that is where the developer relationship is precisely the hedge that we have against any completion risk."
- **Downside resilience, evidenced:** committed client lock-ins cover landlord rental commitments roughly two times over at portfolio level; no single client typically takes more than 30% of a campus; asset-liability mismatch eliminated up to FY29; and "Through every cycle since inception, we have not surrendered a single campus."
- **Pricing headroom held back deliberately:** realisation is INR 181/sq ft while "the closest competitor is almost 10% to 15% higher than our numbers" — a stated, unused lever.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **Seat retention of 74% is the number that will be picked at.** Management's defence is that churn is deliberate portfolio rebalancing and mark-to-market repricing, that occupied seats rose, and that committed occupancy of mature centres remains 92% because replacement tenants are already found. Last year's full-year retention was 80–88% after a similarly weak first half.
- Occupancy dipped to 81% from 82% and is guided to 80–85% for three quarters — new-building fill, but it caps the reported metric during the heaviest growth phase.
- FCF is negative INR 56 cr and OCF/EBITDA fell below 1x. Both are explained by growth investment, but they are the first negative prints since listing.
- Concentration in H2: the guidance depends on Eastbridge and Eastside landing on schedule and pre-fills converting.
- Client-mix transition is deliberate but ongoing — IT/ITES fell from 44% to 35% over three years, and management could not break out call-centre exposure within IT/ITES when asked about AI-driven renewal risk.
- The margin-not-dilutive-at-scale claim has only been tested through one heavy capex quarter.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- The retention/occupancy pair must be read together: a 74% retention number alongside 92% committed occupancy and rising occupied seats means the company is actively repricing legacy tenants out, not losing them involuntarily. The metric will look bad in H1 and recover by year-end, as it did last year.
- VAS is structurally more attractive than it looks because it is take-rate, not resale — no cost sits on the books, so it hits the bottom line directly. It tripled YoY and is explicitly excluded from guidance.
- The GCC revenue already booked understates the opportunity: the services layer for signed GCCs has not started billing because most offices are still under fit-out — "the value accretion of the other services over and above the space will happen… over the next two or three quarters."
- Management is holding back a 10–15% pricing lever versus the nearest competitor, choosing volume and campus fill over rate.
- Landlord mix is ~65% non-institutional / 35% institutional and is expected to stay roughly there — the institutional share is the completion hedge, not the whole strategy.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Risk mitigation] Asset-liability mismatch: committed client lock-in revenue covers landlord lock-in rentals ~2.7x on the mature footprint, ~0.8x on the new footprint and ~2x overall — "No funding gap through FY29". Mature footprint 9.1 Msf at 92% committed occupancy carries committed revenue from clients of INR 47,077 Mn; operational footprint 10.4 Msf at 86% carries INR 53,909 Mn.
- [Risk mitigation] Built-in safeguards: typically no more than ~30% of a centre leased to a single client (cap applies to centres over 0.20 Msf); pricing targets rental revenue of at least 2x rental expense; long-term agreements with both landlords and clients; value pricing to stay preferred partner in downturns.
- [Technology] Proprietary stack runs the full lifecycle — Nexus (AI-led property/market discovery and pricing; 200+ properties evaluated, 4.7 Msf booked), WorkBlock (AI-powered design and standardised digital build; 3.5 Msf+ delivered in a year, 45-60 day go-live) and WorkCtrl (digital operating system for smart building operations, building intelligence and automation, workspace experience and digital service management).
- [Market — third party] Deck cites India office stock ~1,055 Msf growing +6.2% YoY versus India flex stock ~110-114 Msf growing +23-25% YoY (flex stock as of Dec'25) and Smartworks at +44% YoY on 14.5 Msf leased; flex was the #1 occupier at 27% of Q2 2026 leasing, ahead of Technology at 21%. Sources cited: CBRE, Knight Frank, Colliers, Redseer, EY, Nasscom, Bloomberg.
- [Market — third party] AI/GCC tailwind claims: AI workforce inside GCCs 181k (CY2025) → 377k (CY2028P) → 730k (CY2030P); GCCs in India to reach 2,400 by 2030 (~115 new per year) with market size $110 Bn at 14% CAGR (2023-30); GCC leasing ~83 → ~114 Msf by CY2030P and flex rising from 18% to 32% of GCC leasing; ~79 Msf of net-new AI-led demand by CY2030.
- [Client proof points, names masked] A Tier-1 'Big Four' professional services client grew to 5,496 seats across Gurgaon and Jaipur (2.3x); a Fortune 500 biopharmaceuticals client to 927 seats across Bengaluru and Hyderabad (2.5x); a global CX & digital services leader at ~5,400 seats multi-city on ~58-month tenure; "Switzerland's largest financial institution" took the majority of a Smartworks-managed tower in Pune (~162k sq. ft., ~3,400 seats, ~60-month tenure).
- [Entity] Formerly known as Smartworks Coworking Spaces Private Limited; CIN L74900DL2015PLC310656; NSE SMARTWORKS / BSE 544447; registered office Nehru Place, New Delhi, corporate office DLF Phase-5, Gurugram; investor relations handled by EY.
